summary: Into the New York morning, markets look defensive but commodities are split: WTI settled near $82.05 and Brent near $91.40 on Nov 24, gold held near $3,561.90, while equities sit at elevated marks, the S&P 500 near 7,237, Nasdaq near 23,734, and the Dow near 50,019, with VIX still above 26. The dominant rates move is lower nominal yields: the U.S. 10-year at 4.91% and 2-year at 4.63% fell roughly 17 to 19 bp over five sessions, and euro-area benchmarks show the 10-year at 3.22%. FX spots have euro-dollar at 1.0963 and dollar-yen at 159.07, while Scandinavian crosses led, with euro-krone and franc-krone closing through 20-day ranges. Official SOFR printed 3.92% on Nov 23, December SOFR futures imply 4.28%, and the December meeting contract implies about 4.10%. Headlines overnight leaned hawkish in Europe and nervous on metals and AI sentiment. Watch the U.S. third-quarter GDP second estimate and October personal income and outlays at 08:30 today, then the late-November data cluster and the December central-bank meetings.
